unit.why: A minimal narrative: R. Zvi Hirsh of Zhidachov tells a dream in which R. Tanhuma is tried in heaven over a midrash and defends it with an exegesis; the exegesis makes up most of the text.

stories.summary_en: R. Zvi Hirsh of Zhidachov dreamt that R. Tanhuma was brought to judgment in heaven for calling God 'the rich man who answers harshly' to Moses, and that R. Tanhuma justified himself by an acronym reading of 'רב לך' (Ruth and Boaz, the ancestors of the Davidic line, with the remaining letters spelling עזות).
